newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot LPGs weaker amid lower NYMEX values.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot LPGs weaker amid lower NYMEX values.

text.p: U.S. spot liquefied petroleum gas prices were lower in quiet midday trade on Wednesday, partly due to weaker values on NYMEX futures.
"Crude has really softened things here," said one Houston LPG trader.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, Mont Belvieu, Texas, spot propane was down a half cent to between 33.75 cents and 34.00 cents a gallon.
In the Midwest, Conway, Kansas, spot material shed about a quarter to 34.25/34.50 cents.
Players said there was little news apart from crude being taken down by bearish inventory data.
The butane markets were also lower. Belvieu normal was off a half cent at 37.00/37.50 cents and Midwest material was largely steady.
Meanwhile, Amoco Canada said Wednesday it was to build a petrochemical plant that is to start up in 2000.
